Fixes #83532

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
NONE
```

issue_context.title: [migration phase 1] Inject Predicate and Priority Metadata as framework CycleState
issue_context.body:
**What would you like to be added**:
Inject PredicateMetadata and PriorityMetadata, the pre-calculated state for predicate and priorities, as CycleState in the framework.

**Why is this needed**:
This is needed for phase 1 framework migration which requires implementing all predicates/priorities as framework plugins that call back into the predicate/priority functions.

/sig scheduling
/assign

review_comments: Why are we removing `nominatedPods == nil` check?
len(nominatedPods) is zero for a nil nominatedPods, so the check is redundant.
Ok, thanks for explanation
In the future, when we finish the migration, we can move the fields of `PredicateMetadata` here? (right now it holds a pointer pointing to metaCopy)

This is holding a pointer to the PredicatesMetadata that is currently used, note that we copy the CycleState every time we copy meta, and so they are one-to-one all the time.

We need this during phase 1 of the migration phase where we call the predicates/priorities directly and so we need the metadata. In phase 2, this will be removed, metadata producers will be moved to be prefilters, each will write its pre-computed data (e.g., evenpodsspread prefilter will generate and write evenpodsspread pre-computed data), see this PR: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/83286
SG. Thanks for explanation.

why not `Reference predicates.PredicateMetadata`?

Alternatively, you don't need a struct, just the type to which you can add methods. Because go :)

```go
type PredicatesStateData predicates.PredicateMetadata

func (p *PredicatesStateData) Clone() framework.StateData {
    return p
}
```
I did that in the first iteration, but felt I should be consistent with how we deal with priorities metadata.
Can't we do the same for Priorities?

no, it is just an ```interface{}```: the [metadata producer returns a pointer](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/384e03ad92732ac35735e33a43a1391d180bb659/pkg/scheduler/algorithm/priorities/metadata.go#L58). in any case, it does not really matter how we do it.
Why can this happen?
moved it as is from where it was.
You didn't change `TaintToleration` plugin to make use of this metadata because it doesn't need it?
it does not need it, but I think we should do that regardless in case the logic is modified before we get the chance to migrate it to run natively in the plugin. I will do that in a followup PR.
sg
why was it not necessary to clone before?

You mean why move it? or why copy at all? if the former, I wanted to make sure all instances of copy (which is nodeinfo/meta/state) are done in the same place, if the latter, this is needed because nodeInfo gets modified during eviction evaluation inside selectVictimsOnNode
Ok, I realize now that this was moved from inside the other function. Sg.
The comment needs to be updated too regarding the return values
Does this need to fail here or could it aggregate the errors from nominated pods and return that?
I don't think it is useful to do that, if this happen, I don't it matters which nominated pod caused it.
Why is the above line removed?
It doesn't really make sense to compute this in the scheduler directly, we will be exporting a metric that tracks filtering reasons, and from that one can compute any summary statistic they want.
